# `aitbc messaging dm send`

Send an encrypted DM to a recipient who has published a dm_key. Metadata (sender, recipient, size, time) is public by design; only the body is sealed.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc messaging dm send [OPTIONS] RECIPIENT
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recipient` | text | yes | — |

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--wallet` | text | — | yes | Wallet that signs the DM |
| `--message` | text | — | yes | Plaintext body (encrypted before it leaves this process) |
| `--fee` | decimal | `0.01` | no | Transaction fee (AIT) |
| `--confirm` | flag | `false` | no | Seal, sign and submit once (default: dry run) |
| `--rpc-url` | text | — | no | Blockchain RPC URL |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc messaging dm send --wallet <wallet_name> --message <message> RECIPIENT
RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8202/rpc
aitbc messaging dm send --wallet <wallet_name> --message <message> RECIPIENT --rpc-url "$RPC_URL"
```
